# Recipe Recommender

An AI-based recipe recommender. The first feature is a welcome page showing a
**Recipe of the Day** that is generated by AI once per calendar day.

The backend and infrastructure follow the conventions of the `cadence` app
(FastAPI + SQLAlchemy 2.0 + Alembic + Postgres, OpenAI Agents SDK, docker-compose
with a cron sidecar). The frontend follows the visual style of the `react-food-app`
(warm palette, Noto Sans JP, CSS Modules) on a Vite + React + TypeScript stack.

## Architecture

```
recipe-recommender/
├── backend/        FastAPI app (src/recipe_recommender), Alembic migrations, pytest
├── frontend/       Vite + React + TS, TanStack Query, CSS Modules
├── docker-compose.yml   db + backend + frontend + daily cron sidecar
└── .env.example
```

- `GET /api/v1/recipe-of-the-day` — returns today's recipe, generating it on
  demand if it doesn't exist yet (so the app works without the cron job).
- `POST /api/v1/recipe-of-the-day/generate` — cron-guarded (requires the
  `X-Cron-Token` header to match `RECIPE_CRON_TOKEN`). Idempotent per day.

The `recipe_of_the_day` table has a **unique `recipe_date`**, which enforces
"generated once per day" at the database level.

## Running with Docker

```bash
cp .env.example .env
# Optional: set OPENAI_API_KEY for real AI recipes (otherwise the stub is used),
# and set RECIPE_CRON_TOKEN to enable the daily cron job.
docker compose up --build
```

- Frontend: http://localhost:5175
- Backend:  http://localhost:8003 (health at `/health`, docs at `/docs`)
- Postgres: localhost:5436

Without an `OPENAI_API_KEY` (or with `RECIPE_STUB=true`) the app uses a
deterministic stub recipe generator, so the whole stack runs end to end with no
AI credentials.

## Local development (outside Docker)

Backend:

```bash
cd backend
uv sync
uv run alembic upgrade head        # needs a Postgres on DATABASE_URL
uv run uvicorn recipe_recommender.api.app:app --reload
```

Frontend (point the dev proxy at the host backend port):

```bash
cd frontend
npm install
VITE_PROXY_TARGET=http://localhost:8003 npm run dev
```

## Tests

```bash
cd backend && uv run pytest        # needs Postgres (uses TEST_DATABASE_URL)
cd frontend && npm test
```
